intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous mutation in the STX11 gene (605014) on chromosome 6q24.

checks.claim: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous mutation in the STX11 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we found homozygous mutations in STX11 in five consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds
checks.explanation: The paper links FHL4 to 6q24 and reports homozygous STX11 mutations in affected kindreds.

checks.claim: The STX11 gene is located on chromosome 6q24.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage to a 10 cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960 defined a novel FHL locus. By screening positional candidate genes, we identified a homozygous deletion of 5 bp in the syntaxin 11 gene (STX11)
checks.explanation: STX11 was found as a positional candidate in the 6q24 linked region.

paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is an autosomal recessive hyperinflammatory disorder caused by defects in syntaxin-11. Reported patients had fever, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia and hyperferritinemia, together with deficient natural killer (NK) cell activity and degranulation (Muller et al., 2014). Rudd et al. (2006) found that some patients had long disease-free remissions without specific treatment.

checks.claim: FHL4 is an autosomal recessive hyperinflammatory disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hyperactive phagocytes and defects in natural killer cell function.
checks.explanation: The paper describes FHL as autosomal recessive with hyperactive phagocytes, which fits 'hyperinflammatory'.

checks.claim: FHL4 is caused by defects in syntaxin-11.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) type-4 to chromosome 6q24 and identification of mutations in syntaxin 11.
checks.explanation: The title states that FHL type 4 is associated with syntaxin 11 mutations.

checks.claim: Patients with FHL4 reported by Muller et al. (2014) had fever, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia and hyperferritinemia.
checks.evidence_quote: For patient C, it has not been possible to retrieve laboratory parameters at initial presentation.
checks.explanation: The table records these features only for patients A and B; patient C has no data, so the generalisation to all reported patients goes beyond the paper.

checks.claim: Patients with FHL4 reported by Muller et al. (2014) had deficient NK cell activity and degranulation.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients displayed defective lysis of K562 target cells and degranulation by NK cells in response to K562 target cells or engagement of the Fc receptor CD16
checks.explanation: Table also lists NK activity and degranulation as deficient in all three patients.

checks.claim: Rudd et al. (2006) found that some FHL4 patients had long disease-free remissions without specific treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: Three patients experienced long periods (> or = 1 year) in remission without specific treatment, which is very uncommon in this disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports that three STX11-mutated patients had long remissions without specific treatment.

paragraphs.text: zur Stadt et al. (2005) studied a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with 5 children affected with familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL). Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cells of the patients. They also studied 5 more consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds.

paragraphs.text: Rudd et al. (2006) reported 6 children with FHL from 4 unrelated families without perforin mutations who carried STX11 mutations. Three patients had long periods (1 year or more) in remission without specific treatment, which the authors noted is very uncommon in this disease. Some patients developed severe psychomotor retardation. Two of the 6 patients developed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or acute myelogenous leukemia (AML).

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) described 3 children from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families. The authors described them as 2 infants and a 5-year-old child who presented with HLH. Patient A, a boy, had onset at 2 months of age. He had fever, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia (hemoglobin 55 g/L), neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia and hyperferritinemia. Patient B, a boy with onset at 5 years, had the same findings, with a hemoglobin of 71 g/L. Hemophagocytosis and neurologic manifestations were recorded as absent in both boys. Patient C, a girl whose onset was listed at 48 months, presented with a hyperinflammatory syndrome. All 3 patients had deficient NK cell activity and degranulation.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with 5 children affected with FHL, zur Stadt et al. (2005) screened positional candidate genes and identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. They found homozygous STX11 mutations in 5 additional consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds. Two families had the 5-bp deletion. One family had a 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2). Two families had a nonsense mutation causing a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the 5-bp deletion.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) sequenced the coding regions and splice sites of UNC13D, STX11 and STXBP2 in 3 children with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families. All 3 patients were homozygous for a novel missense mutation in STX11, c.173T-C (L58P), located in the Habc domain. Their parents were heterozygous for the mutation and had no recorded history of inflammatory disease. Patient A also carried 2 UNC13D variants. He was heterozygous for a rare c.811C-T (P271S) variant, which he inherited from his father, and homozygous for an uncommon c.2782C-T (R928C) variant. The authors suggested that these UNC13D variants might contribute to the severity of his disease.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) found defective NK cell cytotoxicity and degranulation in patients homozygous for the STX11 L58P mutation, and IL-2 stimulation partly restored both. Expression of perforin, granzyme B and CD107a was normal. Syntaxin-11 levels were greatly reduced in patient PBMCs. Patient LAK cells showed a selective loss of syntaxin-11, while Munc18-2 expression was similar to that of controls. In HEK-293T cells, the syntaxin-11 L58P and N-peptide R4A mutants were expressed at wildtype levels but did not bind Munc18-2. In contrast, the C-terminal Q268X FHL4 mutant still bound Munc18-2. The authors proposed that loss of Munc18-2 binding may destabilize syntaxin-11, which would explain its low expression in patient cells.

paragraphs.text: Locatelli et al. (2020) conducted an open-label, single-group phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone. They treated 34 patients aged 18 years or younger with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis: 27 had been treated before and 7 had not. Of the previously treated patients, 63% had a response, compared with a prespecified null hypothesis of 40%. Seventy percent of them proceeded to transplantation, and 74% were alive at the last observation. Emapalumab was not associated with any organ toxicity. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during treatment, and emapalumab was stopped in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with 5 children affected with FHL4, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. They found it by screening positional candidate genes in the region linked on chromosome 6q24. The same deletion was found in the homozygous state in 2 more consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the deletion.

checks.explanation: The family is the large Kurdish kindred with five affected children.

paragraphs.text: In 3 children with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families, Muller et al. (2014) identified a homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene. It results in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in the Habc domain. The parents were heterozygous for the mutation and had no recorded history of inflammatory disease. The patients had deficient NK cell activity and degranulation, with greatly reduced syntaxin-11 levels in their cells. In HEK-293T cells, the L58P mutant was expressed at wildtype levels but did not bind Munc18-2. One patient was also heterozygous for an UNC13D P271S variant and homozygous for an UNC13D R928C variant, which the authors suggested might contribute to the severity of his disease.
